objective: Computation, explained by ticket A. Record which port relations plane glue presents to atoms, and characterize the two disturbances of the twin rule: the doubled-square line that joins an atom's twin class and the emitting atoms whose lines split by port into twin pairs.
status: Proved by exact computation on 191 spaces (111 census, 80 random with plane glue): through atoms the facing cut is always free; the touching rule holds wherever the removal's side is free (88,764 pairs) and fails only at constrained sides (7,319 of 11,100); glue lines joining an atom's twin class are doubled-square lines meeting two or more of its ports (218); split atoms (64) split by the points of a line they emit into a planar brace and differ only on glue lines
title: What plane glue does
